'''Jean-Philippe Ansermet''' ({{IPA|fr|ɑ̃.sɛʁ.mɛ|lang}}; born {{Birth date|1957|3|1}}) is a Swiss [[physicist]] and [[engineer]] and a professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=ORCID|title=Jean-Philippe Ansermet (0000-0002-1307-4864)|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1307-4864|access-date=2021-01-13|website=orcid.org|language=en}}</ref> His research focuses on the fabrication and properties of [[Nanomaterials|nanostructured materials]] as well as [[spintronics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=LPMN|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lpmn/|access-date=2021-01-13|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Career ==
Jean-Philippe Ansermet graduated from [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] with a degree in [[physics]] in 1980. He then pursued a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], developing [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy|NMR spectroscopy]] for [[catalysis]] research and defending his thesis in 1985.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=A New Approach to the Study of Surface Phenomena: Measurements of Diffusion Rates, Intermolecular Distances and Electronic Properties of Carbon Monoxide Chemisorbed on Supported Platinum Catalysts by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance.|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1985PhDT........64A|date=1985|first=Jean-Philippe|last=Ansermet|bibcode=1985PhDT........64A}}</ref> He then continued his research on surface NMR as a postdoc at the same institution until 1987,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ansermet|first1=Jean-Philippe|last2=Wang|first2=Po-Kang|last3=Slichter|first3=Charles P.|last4=Sinfelt|first4=J. H.|date=1988-02-01|title=NMR study of electronic properties of the chemisorption of CO on supported Pt catalysts|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.37.1417|journal=Physical Review B|volume=37|issue=4|pages=1417–1428|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.37.1417|pmid=9944658|bibcode=1988PhRvB..37.1417A|url-access=subscription}}</ref> when he was named group leader for the Swiss chemical company [[Novartis#Ciba-Geigy|Ciba-Geigy]], working on [[composite material]]s and [[Charge-transfer complex|charge-transfer salts]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Patent for Process for the production of conductive layers Patent (Patent # 5,348,762 issued September 20, 1994) - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/5348762|access-date=2021-02-11|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref> In 1992, he was named professor of experimental physics at EPFL, where he was promoted to full professor in 1995 and named head of the physics section in 2007. There, he teaches classical mechanics as well as thermodynamics to undergraduate and graduate students.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Jean-Philippe Ansermet's page at EPFL|url=https://people.epfl.ch/jean-philippe.ansermet|access-date=13 January 2021|website=epfl.ch}}</ref>

He was a member of the executive committee of the [[European Physical Society]] from 1993 to 1998, and the president of the [[Swiss Physical Society]] from 2002 to 2006.{{citation needed|date=August 2021}}

== Research ==
Ansermet heads the Laboratory of the Physics of Nanostructured Materials at the Institute of Physics of EPFL.<ref name=":0" /> Research in his lab focuses on [[spintronics]] and novel magnetic resonance methods, including sub-THz instrumentation.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Research at the LPMN|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lpmn/research/|access-date=13 January 2021|website=epfl.ch}}</ref>

The laboratory of Ansermet characterized giant magnetoresistance with current driven perpendicular to the interfaces of Co/Cu multilayers before large collaborations could achieve the same through lithography.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Blondel|first1=A.|last2=Meier|first2=J. P.|last3=Doudin|first3=B.|last4=Ansermet|first4=J.‐Ph.|date=1994-12-05|title=Giant magnetoresistance of nanowires of multilayers|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.112495|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=65|issue=23|pages=3019–3021|doi=10.1063/1.112495|bibcode=1994ApPhL..65.3019B|issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It also participated in the discovery that a current can flip the magnetization of a nanostructure ''via'' the [[spin-transfer torque]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wegrowe|first1=J.-E.|last2=Kelly|first2=D.|last3=Jaccard|first3=Y.|last4=Guittienne|first4=Ph|last5=Ansermet|first5=J.-Ph|date=1999-03-01|title=Current-induced magnetization reversal in magnetic nanowires|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/epl/i1999-00213-1/meta|journal=EPL|language=en|volume=45|issue=5|page=626|doi=10.1209/epl/i1999-00213-1|bibcode=1999EL.....45..626W|s2cid=250859071 |issn=0295-5075|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The lab demonstrated the concept of a heat-driven spin torque in [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnetic]] metals.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yu|first1=Haiming|last2=Granville|first2=Simon|last3=Yu|first3=Dapeng|last4=Ansermet|first4=Jean-Philippe|date=2010-04-12|title=Evidence for thermal spin transfer torque|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=104|issue=14|article-number=146601|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.146601|pmid=20481950|arxiv=1003.3042|bibcode=2010PhRvL.104n6601Y|s2cid=15412728}}</ref> Using thermodynamics, the laboratory also predicted and demonstrated a heat-driven spin torque in insulating ferromagnet.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brechet|first1=Sylvain D.|last2=Vetro|first2=Francesco A.|last3=Papa|first3=Elisa|last4=Barnes|first4=Stewart E.|last5=Ansermet|first5=Jean-Philippe|date=2013-08-22|title=Evidence for a Magnetic Seebeck Effect|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.087205|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=111|issue=8|article-number=087205|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.087205|pmid=24010472|arxiv=1306.1001|bibcode=2013PhRvL.111h7205B|s2cid=14013887}}</ref>

The laboratory of Ansermet studies [[Dynamic nuclear polarization|Dynamic Nuclear Polarization (DNP)]] as a way to enhance signals in surface-NMR experiments,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ansermet|first1=J. -Ph.|last2=Slichter|first2=C. P.|last3=Sinfelt|first3=J. H.|date=1990-01-01|title=Solid state NMR techniques for the study of surface phenomena|journal=Progress in Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy|language=en|volume=22|issue=5|pages=401–421|doi=10.1016/0079-6565(90)80005-3|issn=0079-6565}}</ref> requiring excitation in the sub-THz domain. This constraint led to the development of DNP instruments by the LPMN and its collaborators and the creation the Swiss start-up Swissto12. Collaboration between the Swiss Plasma Center at EPFL and the LPMN led to the construction of a [[gyrotron]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Alberti|first1=S.|last2=Braunmueller|first2=F.|last3=Tran|first3=T. M.|last4=Genoud|first4=J.|last5=Hogge|first5=J-Ph.|last6=Tran|first6=M. Q.|last7=Ansermet|first7=J-Ph.|date=2013-11-12|title=Nanosecond Pulses in a THz Gyrotron Oscillator Operating in a Mode-Locked Self-Consistent $Q$-Switch Regime|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.205101|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=111|issue=20|article-number=205101|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.205101|pmid=24289692|bibcode=2013PhRvL.111t5101A|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The laboratory further showed that this equipment can induce resonance in antiferromagnets, thus expanding the field of [[spintronics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Białek|first1=M.|last2=Magrez|first2=A.|last3=Murk|first3=A.|last4=Ansermet|first4=J.-Ph.|date=2018-02-12|title=Spin-wave resonances in bismuth orthoferrite at high temperatures|journal=Physical Review B|volume=97|issue=5|article-number=054410|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.97.054410|bibcode=2018PhRvB..97e4410B|s2cid=125317870 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
* Secretary of the [[European Physical Society]] (1993-1998)<ref>{{Cite journal|last=|first=|date=|title=Views From Presidents Kroo and Schopper|url=https://cdn.ymaws.com/www.eps.org/resource/resmgr/about_us/eps_40_years_n_kroo_and_h_sc.pdf|journal=Europhysics News|volume=|pages=|via=}}</ref>
* President of the [[Swiss Physical Society]] (2002-2006)<ref>{{Cite web|last=SPG-SPS-SSP|title=Centennial|url=https://www.sps.ch/en/events/centennial/|access-date=2021-01-13|website=Schweizerische Physikalische Gesellschaft|language=en-EN}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (2011)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Testa|first=Andrea|date=12 August 2011|title=Jean-Philippe Ansermet named Fellow of the APS|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/jean-philippe-ansermet-named-fellow-of-the-aps-2/|access-date=13 January 2021|website=}}</ref>
